variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Scientific machine learning, or scientific ML, combines learned models with knowledge about a scientific system. That knowledge may include governing equations, conservation laws, symmetries, units, geometry, boundary conditions, numerical solvers, or carefully designed experiments.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Frame the scientific decision before choosing a model”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Forward surrogate
pairs.detail: Predict a field or response from parameters, initial state, and boundary conditions.
pairs.explanation: Predict a field or response from parameters, initial state, and boundary conditions. The surrogate earns its place when repeated predictions are faster at matched accuracy.

pairs.label: Inverse model
pairs.detail: Estimate parameters, sources, or initial conditions from incomplete observations.
pairs.explanation: Estimate parameters, sources, or initial conditions from incomplete observations. Identifiability and posterior uncertainty matter as much as point error.

pairs.label: Hybrid simulator
pairs.detail: Keep a numerical or mechanistic core and learn an unresolved closure, correction, or constitutive relation.
pairs.explanation: Keep a numerical or mechanistic core and learn an unresolved closure, correction, or constitutive relation. The learned term needs explicit units and validity bounds.

pairs.label: Experiment policy
pairs.detail: Rank simulations or physical experiments by information gain, cost, safety, and coverage of uncertain regimes rather than sampling blindly.
pairs.explanation: Rank simulations or physical experiments by information gain, cost, safety, and coverage of uncertain regimes rather than sampling blindly.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. A learned approximation is not evidence of a scientific discovery by itself.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Forward surrogate: Predict a field or response from parameters, initial state, and boundary conditions. Inverse model: Estimate parameters, sources, or initial conditions from incomplete observations. Hybrid simulator: Keep a numerical or mechanistic core and learn an unresolved closure, correction, or constitutive relation. Experiment policy: Rank simulations or physical experiments by information gain, cost, safety, and coverage of uncertain regimes rather than sampling blindly.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Scientific machine learning, or scientific ML, combines learned models with knowledge about a scientific system. That knowledge may include governing equations, conservation laws, symmetries, units, geometry, boundary conditions, numerical solvers, or carefully designed experiments.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose where scientific structure enters the model”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Data-driven surrogate
pairs.detail: Learn inputs to outputs from simulations or observations.
pairs.explanation: Learn inputs to outputs from simulations or observations. This is often simple to train, but coverage and extrapolation boundaries must be explicit.

pairs.label: Soft-constrained model
pairs.detail: Add equation residuals, conservation terms, boundary losses, or symmetry penalties.
pairs.explanation: Add equation residuals, conservation terms, boundary losses, or symmetry penalties. Every term needs compatible scaling and separate validation.

pairs.label: Hard-constrained model
pairs.detail: Use coordinates, parameterizations, equivariant layers, or projection operators that make selected violations impossible by construction.
pairs.explanation: Use coordinates, parameterizations, equivariant layers, or projection operators that make selected violations impossible by construction.

pairs.label: Neural operator
pairs.detail: Learn a family of solution operators across forcing, coefficients, or initial conditions instead of fitting one finite-dimensional solution.
pairs.explanation: Learn a family of solution operators across forcing, coefficients, or initial conditions instead of fitting one finite-dimensional solution.

pairs.label: Hybrid correction
pairs.detail: Run a mechanistic solver and learn only a closure or discrepancy term.
pairs.explanation: Run a mechanistic solver and learn only a closure or discrepancy term. Stability and coupling behavior must be tested end to end.

pairs.label: Probabilistic model
pairs.detail: Predict a distribution, ensemble, or posterior when observations cannot identify one answer.
pairs.explanation: Predict a distribution, ensemble, or posterior when observations cannot identify one answer. Calibration is evaluated empirically by regime.

variants.prompt: Why is a random row split often weak evidence for a scientific surrogate?
options: It always makes the training set too small
Nearby states from one trajectory or simulation can leak across splits while entire regimes remain untested
It prevents automatic differentiation
It can only be used with classification models
variants.explanation: Scientific samples are commonly correlated by trajectory, experiment, geometry, time, or parameter regime. Grouped regime-level splits better test the intended claim.

variants.prompt: A weighted training loss falls, but the boundary-condition error rises above its release limit. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The lower total proves the model improved
The boundary term can be ignored when data error is low
The candidate fails the scientific evidence ledger even though the scalar objective improved
The model only needs more inference hardware
variants.explanation: A weighted sum can hide deterioration in a critical component. Every scientific constraint must remain visible and meet its own acceptance limit.

variants.prompt: An uncertainty interval achieves its target empirical coverage but is wider than the decision tolerance. What should the release gate conclude?

The interval is calibrated enough but not useful enough for that decision

Treat the interval midpoint as exact
